topics.definition: A data structure is a way of organizing and storing data so it can be used efficiently.
topics.example: An array stores elements in contiguous memory.
tips: Choose the right data structure for better performance.

topics.definition: An algorithm is a step-by-step procedure to solve a problem.
tips: Algorithms should be correct and efficient.

topics.definition: Data structures are mainly Linear and Non-Linear.
tips: Understand when to use each type.

topics.definition: Time complexity measures how the execution time grows with input size.
tips: Lower complexity usually means faster algorithms.

topics.definition: Space complexity measures the memory used by an algorithm.
tips: Optimize both time and space when possible.

topics.definition: Big-O represents the upper bound (worst-case) time complexity.

topics.example: Linear Search when item is first

topics.definition: Big-Theta represents the tight bound of an algorithm.
tips: Used when upper and lower bounds are the same.

topics.definition: Linear structures store elements sequentially, while non-linear structures use hierarchical or network relationships.
DSA improves efficiency, reduces execution time and helps solve complex problems.
topics.example: Using Binary Search instead of Linear Search
tips: Essential for coding interviews and software development.
